name: The Ferreira-Okonkwo Silence — Feed Dark, 2207
creator: Inadvertent — triggered by Axiom Network One technical failure during live coverage of the Meridian Compact ratification vote
description: On the night of March 14, 2207, every Axiom Network One neural feed went dark for eleven minutes and forty-two seconds during the live broadcast of the Meridian Compact ratification vote — the single largest simultaneous BCI audience in GLMZ history, estimated at 4.2 million concurrent feeds. Into that silence, a pirate signal from RED STATIC broadcast an uncut, seventeen-minute documentary — later attributed to journalist Peculiar Osadebay-Strömberg — revealing that three of the seven Compact signatories had pre-signed loyalty amendments binding them to Axiom workforce arbitration clauses buried in the charter's annexes. When Axiom feeds restored, the documentary had already propagated through 800,000 secondary BCI caches and could not be fully recalled.
medium: neural feed (involuntary — all BCI tiers); pirate signal overlay; secondary cache propagation
cultural_impact: The Silence became the definitive proof-of-concept that corponation media blackouts create the exact vacuum that pirate networks are designed to fill — after 2207, RED STATIC's subscriber base tripled within six months, and 'eleven forty-two' entered Meridian slang as shorthand for any moment of accidental institutional transparency.
controversy: Axiom Network One publicly attributed the outage to cascade failure in a legacy switching node and denied any knowledge of the pirate override; an internal audit leaked in 2209 suggested the blackout was triggered by a deliberate inside actor whose identity was never confirmed. Osadebay-Strömberg was never formally charged but lost all Tier 3-4 press credentials within the year.
story_hooks: A player character was one of the 800,000 whose BCI cached the full documentary — years later, a corporate fixer arrives at their door asking them to voluntarily submit to a cache wipe in exchange for a substantial Quanta payment, or else.

The inside actor who triggered the blackout has never been identified; they are still alive, still inside Axiom's infrastructure division, and they just made contact with someone who is investigating the Compact's current enforcement clauses.

A Tier 2 archivist has spent years assembling every secondary-cache fragment of the original Osadebay-Strömberg documentary — the version that propagated was edited; she believes the uncut cut contains a name that was stripped before broadcast, and she needs someone to help her find the source node.
